summary: Receives OpenVR SDK sensor, projection, tracker, frame timing, action, and hand skeleton data as CHOP channels.
key_concepts: OpenVR CHOP is a Windows-only OpenVR SDK CHOP for headset, controller, tracker, frame timing, action, and skeleton channels.
Output mode switches among sensors, projection matrices, trackers, frame timings, actions, and skeletons.
Projection modes use near, far, and unit-scale settings, with OpenVR units expressed in meters before scaling.
Tracker output can be limited by maximum tracker count and first tracker index for multi-tracker rigs.
Custom actions use an OpenVR action manifest, while legacy names exist only for compatibility with older files.
If an OpenVR TOP is present, TouchDesigner playback is throttled to the VR device refresh rate; tracker-only projects can otherwise sample faster.

common_gotchas: Official docs list this operator as Windows-only.
If any OpenVR TOP exists in the project, playback is throttled to the VR device refresh rate.
Without OpenVR TOP, controller/tracker-only projects can sample tracking at higher rates for non-VR uses.
OpenVR units are meters by default; set Unit Scale when the scene uses another scale.
Custom action channels depend on the OpenVR Actions manifest; legacy channel naming should stay off unless loading older files.
Finger Tip Bones are no longer supported in OpenVR skeleton output according to the docs.
